newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: LARGEST CZECH EXPORTER SAYS DEVALUATION NOT ANSWER.
newsitem.headline: LARGEST CZECH EXPORTER SAYS DEVALUATION NOT ANSWER.

text.p: Skoda Auto a.s., the largest Czech exporter, on Thursday said that it was not seeking a devaluation of the crown to boost sales abroad.

Speaking at company's annual presentation to the press, outgoing Vice-chairman Volkhard Kohler said that while the company could still do more in squeezing out efficiencies and productivity, it did not see a devaluation as a way to boost foreign sales.
"For sure you haven't heard us crying for a devaluation," he said.
Skoda, a unit of Volkswagen AG accounted for roughly five percent of total Czech exports in 1996 and said that number could rise to 7-8 percent in the coming years.
Other Czech exporters, however, are struggling as the country's current account balance, due to a burgeoning trade deficit, grew to over eight percent of GDP in 1996.

Some have argued that a devaluation of the crown would help boost exports, but the central bank and government officials have steadfastly ruled out any such move, often holding Skoda up as an example of how companies must become more efficient before worrying about a devaluation.
Skoda, however, also imports many components for its assembly plant north of Prague.
The trade deficit hit a record 160.3 billion crowns in 1996, and is expected to rise further to about 215 billion in 1997.
